```{r, results="hide", echo=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(error=FALSE)
if (!exists(".version")) {
    .version <- package_version("1.0")
}
```

```{r, results="asis", echo=FALSE}
cat("# Data frame (", as.character(.version), ")", sep="")
```

## Overview

The `data_frame` format provides an on-disk representation of a **data frame**.
This is a columnar data format where each column is of the same length (or height, for more complex columns),
and the $i$-th row of the **data frame** consists of the $i$-th entry of each column.
It is based on the `DataFrame` class from the [**S4Vectors** Bioconductor package](https://bioconductor.org/packages/S4Vectors).

## Object metadata

The `OBJECT` file should contain a `data_frame` property, itself a JSON object with the following properties:

- `version`, a string specifying the version of the `data_frame` format.
```{r, results="asis", echo=FALSE}
cat("  This should be set to \"", as.character(.version), "\".", sep="")
```

## Directory structure

### Contents 

The directory should contain the following:

- `OBJECT`, a JSON file as described above.
- `basic_columns.h5`, a HDF5 file.

Optionally, it may also contain:

- `other_columns/`, a subdirectory.
- `element_annotations/`, a subdirectory.
- `other_annotations/`, a subdirectory.

### `basic_columns.h5`

#### General

The `basic_columns.h5` file should contain an `data_frame` group.

The `data_frame` group should have a `row-count` attribute.
This should be scalar and its datatype should be representable by a 64-bit unsigned integer.
The value of this attribute specifies the number of rows in the **data frame**.

The `data_frame` group should contain `column_names`, a 1-dimensional string dataset containing the column names of the **data frame**.
The length of this dataset defines the number of columns of the **data frame**.
Column names should not be empty or duplicated.

Optionally, the `data_frame` group may optionally contain `row_names`, a 1-dimensional string dataset containing the row names of the **data frame** if any are present.
The length of this dataset should be equal to the number of rows in the **data frame**.
The dataset may contain empty or duplicated strings.
(This is more relaxed than the column names as the row names are considered to be descriptive rather than structural aspects of the **data frame**.)

The `data_frame` group should contain the `data` group that stores all "basic" columns.
Each basic column is represented by a HDF5 group or dataset that is named after the positional index of the column in the **data frame**,
i.e., the $i$-th column is represented by a group/dataset at `data_frame/data/{i}`.
See the following sections on the supported representations of each basic column.

```{r, results="asis", echo=FALSE}
if (.version < package_version("1.1")) {
cat("#### Non-factor column")
} else {
cat("#### Non-factor, non-compressed VLS column")
}
```

If the $i$-th column in the **data frame** is not a
```{r, results="asis", echo=FALSE}
if (.version < package_version("1.1")) {
cat('factor,')
} else {
cat('factor or compressed VLS type,')
}
```
it should represented by a HDF5 dataset at `data_frame/data/{i}`.
This dataset should be a 1-dimensional and of length equal to the number of rows in the **data frame**.

The `data_frame/data/{i}` dataset should have a `type` scalar string attribute.
The value of the `type` attribute can be one of `"integer"`, `"boolean"`, `"number"` or `"string"`.
The set of acceptable datatypes of the dataset is determined by the value of `type`:

- For `type = "integer"` or `"boolean"`, the datatype should be representable by a 32-bit signed integer.
- For `type = "number"`, the datatype should be representable by a 64-bit float.
- For `type = "string"`, a string datatype should be used.

Optionally, for `type = "string"`, the `data_frame/data/{i}` dataset may contain a `format` scalar string attribute.
The attribute should contain one of the following values:

- `"none"`: no constraints on the contents of each string in the dataset.
  This is the default behaviour if no `format` is present.
- `"date"`: strings should be dates following a `YYYY-MM-DD` format.
- `"date-time"`: strings should be Internet Date/Time values following the format described in [RFC3339](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3339).

Optionally, the the `data_frame/data/{i}` dataset may have a `missing-value-placeholder` attribute. 
If present, all entries in the dataset equal to the placeholder value should be treated as missing.
The datatype of the attribute should be the same as the dataset if `type != "string"`, or any string datatype if `type = "string"`.

### Factor column

If the $i$-th column in the **data frame** is a factor, it should be represented by a HDF5 group at `data_frame/data/{i}`.
This group should have a `type` scalar string attribute containing the `"factor"` value.

The `data_frame/data/{i}` group should contain `levels`, a 1-dimensional string dataset containing the factor levels.
All levels should be unique, so the length of this dataset determines the number of factor levels.
Missing values are not supported.

The `data_frame/data/{i}` group should contain `codes`, a 1-dimensional dataset containing the 0-indexed factor codes. 
The length of this dataset should be equal to the number of rows in the **data frame**.
The datatype should be representable by a 64-bit unsigned integer.
Entries of this dataset should be less than the number of levels, or equal to the missing placeholder value if a `missing-value-placeholder` attribute is present. 

Optionally, the `data_frame/data/{i}/codes` dataset may have a `missing-value-placeholder` attribute.
If present, all entries in the dataset equal to the placeholder value should be treated as missing.
The attribute should be scalar and have the same datatype as `data_frame/data/{i}/codes`.

Optionally, the `data_frame/data/{i}` group may have an `ordered` attribute.
This should be scalar and its datatype should be representable by a 32-bit signed integer.
If present, a non-zero value indicates that the factor levels should be treated as ordered.
Otherwise, the levels are treated as unordered.

```{r, results="asis", echo=FALSE}
if (.version >= package_version("1.1")) {
    cat('#### Compressed VLS column

If the $i$-th column in the **data frame** uses the compressed variable length string format, it should be represented by a HDF5 group at `data_frame/data/{i}`.
This group should have a `type` scalar string attribute that contains the `"vls"` value.
See ["Compressed variable-length strings"](../compressed_vls.md) for the specification of the CVLS format.
The CVLS datasets should be stored in the `data_frame/data/{i}` group, and the `data_frame/data/{i}/pointers` dataset should be 1-dimensional.
')
}
```

#### Non-basic columns

If the $i$-th column is not a basic column, it should not be present in the `data_frame/data` group, i.e., `data_frame/data/{i}` should not exist.
Rather, the contents of this column will be stored in the [`other_columns/{i}/` subdirectory](#other_columns).
This is typically used for columns consisting of more complex data structures, e.g., nested **data frame** objects.

### `other_columns/`

The `other_column/` subdirectory stores all "non-basic" columns that cannot be stored directly in the `basic_columns.h5` file.

If the $i$-th column is a non-basic column, it is represented by a subdirectory named after its positional index, i.e., `other_columns/{i}/`.
This subdirectory should contain a child object that has a concept of "height".
The height of this child object should be equal to the number of rows in the **data frame**.
For example, a non-basic column might be a nested **data frame** that has the same number of rows as the enclosing **data frame**.

Each column in the **data frame** should be represented exactly once across `basic_columns.h5` and `other_columns`.
Thus, if a HDF5 dataset or group is present at `data_frame/data/{i}`, there should not be a `other_columns/{i}/` subdirectory, and vice versa.

Aside from the subdirectories corresponding to non-basic columns, no other files or directories should be present in the `other_columns/` subdirectory.
The exception is that of files/directories prefixed with `.` or `_`, which are ignored.

If no `other_columns/` directory is present, it can be assumed that there are no non-basic columns in the **data frame**.

### `element_annotations/`

The `element_annotations/` subdirectory should contain a child object that satisfies the `DATA_FRAME` interface.
This child object should have number of rows equal to the number of columns, i.e., the length of the `data_frame/column_names` dataset in `basic_columns.h5`.
Each row of this child object corresponds to a column of the **data frame** and contains additional annotations for that column.

If this subdirectory is absent, no additional additions are available for columns of the **data frame**.

### `other_annotations/`

The `other_annotations/` subdirectory should contain a child object that satisfies the `SIMPLE_LIST` interface.
This child object holds extra annotations for the entire **data frame**.

If this subdirectory is absent, no extra additions are available for the **data frame**.

## Height

The height of the **data frame** is defined as the number of rows, as specified in the `row-count` attribute of `basic_columns.h5`.

## Dimensions

The dimensions of the **data frame** is defined as the number of rows (`row-count`) and columns (the length of `column_names`).

## Interfaces

The `data_frame` specification satisfies the `DATA_FRAME` interface.
